newsitem.title: USA: US lawmakers propose to curb unsolicited loans.
newsitem.headline: US lawmakers propose to curb unsolicited loans.

text.p: Lenders would be prohibited from sending consumers unsolicited loans that look like checks under legislation proposed Wednesday in the House of Representatives.
Democrats Maurice Hinchey of New York and Henry Gonzalez of Texas introduced the bill, the Unsolicited Loan Consumer Protection Act of 1997, to curb the growing trend.
"Banks should not be sending unsolicited loans through the mail where anyone can get their hands on them," Hinchey said.
"Even if the loan check reaches its target, a trusting individual could sign it and wind up liable for an exorbitant amount," he added.

The bill would amend the Truth in Lending Act to prohibit any creditor from sending a check or other negotiable financial instrument through the mail unless a consumer had applied or requested such a loan.
The bill would also insulate consumers from fraudulent loans. The creditor would bear the burden of proof if a consumer denied having cashed the loan check.
A subcommittee of the House Banking Committee is expected to hold hearings later in the summer on the proposal, congressional staffers said.

One company singled out by the lawmakers was Signet Banking Corp. The company mailed an "instant check loan" to one of Rep. Hinchey's constituents in the amount of $7,500 with a 13.99 percent rate of interest.
"Simply deposit this check today and in minutes you will enjoy the smartest, simplest, most convenient loan available," the offer read.
The company defended its instant loans as proper and good for consumers.
The instant loan offers clearly disclose all relevent information and terms, a Signet spokeswoman said.

"Solicitation materials are written in plain English so that consumers can understand this is a loan," the spokeswoman said. "We believe the proposed legislation will limit consumers' choice in the marketplace."
Consumers would not be liable for repaying the loan if a criminal cashed the check, the spokeswoman said. Signet has loaned almost $1 billion through the instant loan program in the last 12 months.
The proposed legislation is modeled after a law enacted in 1970 prohibiting the practice of sending unsolicited credit cards through the mail.
